phase.goal: PHASE 1 — INTELLIGENCE, BUSINESS FOUNDATION, TRUST ARCHITECTURE, AND PREMIUM EXPERIENCE

milestone.description: Level 3 independent phase-exit review accepted (round 2, EV-0047) — Phase 1 complete

completed: P1-01 through P1-11 (see execution/reviews/level3/phase-1/PHASE_1_COMPLETION_REPORT.md for the full evidence-backed breakdown)

P1-EXIT: Phase 1 evidence package assembled, Level 3 independent review conducted (round 1: revise, 3 defects found and reproduced live; fixes applied with regression tests; round 2: accept, independently re-verified)
deferred: Phase 2: full-stack generation, Blueprint Engine, Build Planner, Component Registry, structured renderer, conversational editing, mobile output (Master Spec §54-59)
Phase 3: live billing, real AI provider connections, production deployment, store submission, continuous governance monitoring (Master Spec §60-66)

testStatus.e2e: pass (6/6, independently re-verified by the Level 3 reviewer from a genuinely fresh/unseeded environment)

knownLimitations: No settings page, integrations-connection UI, or policy-document UI yet — not required by §51's first customer flow.
No real payment provider webhooks exist to drive the billing state machine in production — Phase 3 scope (§62). No real integration provider is connected to the credential vault yet.

AI provider is mock-only; Requirements Engine, Business Model Brief, and unit economics are deterministic/template-based, not real product or market intelligence — correctly disclosed via Truth Status.
Phase 1's own customer flow (§51) never requires generating a Blueprint/Build Plan or a full-stack application; that is explicitly Phase 2 scope (§54-59) and is not implemented.

Steps of the Official V1 Acceptance Test (§67) beyond Phase 1's own exit criteria (export, deployment, store submission, billing-failure simulation, governance-change workflow) are correctly out of scope for Phase 1.
Visual design is functional but not pixel-polished 'premium' — clean typography/spacing, no custom illustration or animation.
Product Knowledge graph only exercises REQUIREMENT/WORKFLOW node types so far; no generation system yet produces Screen/Action/DataModel nodes (Phase 2 concern).
nextAction: Begin Phase 2: decompose into dependency-aware implementation units traceable to Master Spec §54-59 and phase exit criteria (§59), starting with the versioned Blueprint Engine and Component Registry that the Phase 1 Product Knowledge relationship graph was built to support.
